decisions.reason: “Blacker” preserves the eye’s deep pitch-black color without adding the baseline’s “in existence.”
“Seams” naturally conveys the countless hidden structures in the space.
“Come face-to-face” keeps the sense while making the phrasing more natural.
“Cut through dozens of layers” preserves the strike’s effect and the magic’s layered construction.
The recast keeps the developing ability to sense qi and applies it to the monster.
“Fell on him” makes clear that the force struck Jin from above.
“Anticipate” preserves the meaning of expecting the attack.
The recast keeps the sliced-up ground and Jin’s evasion without changing the action.
Naming Morgoth clarifies whose voice continues without changing the viewpoint.
“Weak emotion” directly conveys how Morgoth regarded fear.
“Refusing to face” preserves the sense that he had been avoiding the truth.
The source says the magic is surrounding him now; SOL drops that timing cue.
The recast preserves that Morgoth’s courtesy served his own dignity, not his opponent.
SOL drops the contemptuous address in “네놈”; BASE preserves that attitude with “you bastard.”
“Within a radius … around” states the area clearly, and “him” keeps Jin as the target.
The source describes a piercing sound, singular; SOL changes it to multiple whistles.
“Stems” and “from end to end” express the vines’ thickness and the thorns covering them.
The reordered sentence keeps the contrast with sunlight and the vines’ power.
The source includes a sharp sound before he steadies his breathing; deleting it drops that beat.
SOL adds that he stepped forward, a direction not specified in the source.
“Reaching the edge of its realm” reflects the source’s image of approaching the realm’s limit.
The recast preserves the line expanding into a vast circle.
SOL carries the ash and embers into the following sentence rather than dropping the image.
The source says Jin stood tall and alone; SOL drops the emphasis on his upright, imposing stance.
SOL drops the comparison between the spells’ power and the dazzling flashes; BASE retains it.
The source specifies one direction; SOL changes this to one place.
“A weight of dozens of tons” preserves the force, and the revised sentence reads naturally.
“Shining down on” keeps the spells’ light falling on Jin.
The source imagines Jin standing there instead of Morgoth; “left standing” adds a survival or victory implication.
“Those were different” correctly agrees with the two aspects being compared.
The possessive recast preserves the comparison and avoids the baseline’s awkward phrasing.
The recast keeps the difference in their power as the reason the battle and the world’s fate were decided.
SOL omits the source’s paired actions of emptying and pouring out his power.
The recast preserves both reasons for the Breath’s reduced range and destructive power.
“Resilient” conveys the hero’s toughness without turning 강인 into a direct power ranking.
The source says the power finally became a flash; SOL drops that timing and culmination.
“D immer than usual” preserves the contrast with his normal state in natural English.
“Caught in a sensation” keeps the sense without the unnatural “captured by.”
“The meaning of those two characters” preserves the No-self reference without the awkward “contained in.”
The recast preserves that he experiences again a sensation absent since that day.
